channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan and Rosatom Discuss Potential Small Nuclear Power Plant Construction
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources met with a Rosatom representative to discuss bilateral cooperation in energy, including the feasibility of building small nuclear power plants. They exchanged views on technical, economic, and environmental aspects, as well as safety and training.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expands High-Speed Internet Access to Remote Villages
item.description: Residents of remote and hard-to-reach villages in Kazakhstan are gaining access to high-speed internet through satellite connections. This year, satellite equipment was installed in 12 settlements, with plans for four more by year-end. The project aims to improve education, remote work, and access to public services.

item.title: Bishkek Allocates One Hectare of Arable Land for Judicial Department Building
item.description: The Kyrgyz Cabinet of Ministers has approved the transformation of one hectare of irrigated arable land in Bishkek's Oktyabrsky district for the construction of an administrative building for the Chuy Regional Department of the Judicial Department. The land will be reclassified from agricultural to settlement land.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Employment Rates for Those Over 60 Differ Significantly by Gender
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, 62.5% of men aged 60-64 are employed, compared to 27.3% of women in the same age group. This disparity is highlighted in a new report on aging. The study emphasizes the need for equal employment opportunities, vocational training, and protection against age and gender discrimination for older adults.

item.title: Three Schoolgirls Arrested in Almaty for Alleged Drug Courier Activities
item.description: Three schoolgirls, including a 12-year-old, have been detained in Almaty on suspicion of storing and distributing drugs. Preliminary information suggests they worked as drug couriers, leaving illicit substances in hidden locations. Investigations are ongoing, and similar arrests have occurred in Rudny involving young men and a warehouse worker.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Bank Analysts Model Inflation Above Target for 15 Years
item.description: Analysts at Kazakhstan's National Bank have developed a model for calculating the fundamental yield curve of government securities. The model assumes inflation will slow to 6.5% and remain at that level for 15 years, exceeding the regulator's official target. This study does not reflect the National Bank's official position.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Collects Over 385 Million Som from Transport Control in 10 Months
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, over 384.895 million som were collected for the republican budget from transport control in January-October 2026. Approximately 740,000 vehicles were inspected, with 12,457 violations identified, a 56.36% increase compared to the same period last year. The Ministry of Transport and Communications reported the figures.

item.title: New Power Generation Projects Launched in Zhanaozen, Kazakhstan
item.description: In Zhanaozen, Kazakhstan, a hybrid power plant complex with a capacity of 247 MW, including a 120 MW gas power plant, has been commissioned. This project, a collaboration between KazMunayGas and Italy's Eni S.p.A., aims to ensure energy surplus by 2029 and attract investment. The complex integrates solar, gas, and wind energy.

item.title: Astana's taxi fares higher than Moscow and Beijing, study finds
item.description: A study comparing taxi fares and fuel costs in 16 capital cities reveals that Astana's minimum taxi fare is 500 tenge, with each kilometer costing the same. While fuel is cheaper than in many capitals, taxi rides are more expensive than in Tashkent, Bishkek, and Dushanbe.

item.title: Jambyl athletes honored for achievements at Asian Games
item.description: Athletes from Jambyl region who competed in the 20th Asian Summer Games and 5th Asian Para Games were honored by regional authorities. The athletes secured 6 silver and 1 bronze medal in 12 sports. Notably, judoka Eldos Smetov, a multiple Olympic medalist, was among those recognized.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Defense Minister Inspects Military Units in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Defense Minister Ruslan Mukambetov met with personnel of military units and institutions in Bishkek. He visited the Kyrgyz National Military Lyceum and familiarized himself with the activities of several military units stationed in the Bishkek garrison. During the meetings, service conditions, daily activities, and urgent issues requiring resolution were discussed.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Woman Attacked with Acid Seeks Free Plastic Surgery
item.description: A 42-year-old woman from Shymkent, Kazakhstan, is seeking free plastic surgery after being doused with acid by her ex-husband. She sustained chemical burns to her face and neck, affecting her ability to eat and move. While awaiting scar maturation for potential reconstructive surgery, which may take up to a year, her family is struggling to find a surgeon in Kazakhstan and cannot afford treatment abroad. She is receiving psychological support.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Grants Tax Authorities Power to Suspend Cash Registers Due to Sanction Risks
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's tax authorities can now suspend electronic invoice system accounts and deregister cash registers if sanction risks are identified. This measure, formalized by a government decree, aims to protect economic and financial stability. The changes are in response to a presidential directive on sanction policy.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers New Electricity Tariffs for Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Energy is proposing changes to electricity tariffs for electric vehicle charging stations. The ministry aims to differentiate between commercial charging services and private use. A special tariff will apply to businesses offering EV charging, while private users will pay according to their consumer category.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Building Nearly 50 Small and Medium Hydropower Plants
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is currently constructing approximately 50 small and medium-sized hydropower plants, according to the Energy Minister. In the past five years, around 50 similar plants have been commissioned. The country is also modernizing the Toktogul HPP, increasing its capacity, and proceeding with the strategic Kambar-Ata-1 HPP project.

item.title: Afghanistan: Kunar forest fire extinguished after burning 100 hectares
item.description: A wildfire in the Kunar province of Afghanistan has been contained after burning approximately 100 hectares of forest. The fire, which started in the Nari district, destroyed juniper, oak, and cypress trees. Two children died and their father was injured in the incident.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Diplomat and historian Rustem Kurmangozhin passes away
item.description: Rustem Kurmangozhin, a diplomat and candidate of historical sciences, has suddenly passed away. He graduated from the Moscow State Institute of International Relations in 1985 and served in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs until 2013, reaching the rank of counselor-envoy. He contributed to shaping Kazakhstan's foreign policy.

item.title: Armenian PM hints at potential full withdrawal of Russian border guards
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has not ruled out the possibility of Russian border guards fully withdrawing from the country in the coming years. He expressed gratitude for their service but stated that Armenia should assume full responsibility for border protection. Russian border guards have already completed their service at Yerevan's Zvartnots International Airport and will leave border posts with Iran and Turkey by early 2025.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Calls TikTok a 'Brain-Killing' App, Especially for Youth
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has described TikTok as a 'terrible thing that kills the brain,' particularly affecting young people. Speaking at an AI conference in Moscow, he emphasized that smartphones, when used properly, can be tools for earning money, even in rural areas, advocating for a 'people's digital economy' through education.

item.title: Rogun Hydropower Plant Employs Over 20,000, Dominated by Five Major Employers
item.description: As of August 2026, the Rogun Hydropower Plant project employed 20,563 people across 50 organizations. Approximately 70% of the workforce is concentrated within the five largest employers. Tajik company TGEM is the biggest employer, accounting for 42.6% of the total workforce, primarily involved in construction on the right bank.

item.title: Kuwait Reports Iranian Drone Attacks Targeting Vital Facilities, Four Injured
item.description: Kuwait's Ministry of Defense announced on Thursday that at least four people were injured after intercepting Iranian drones targeting "vital facilities." The ministry stated that the injured were transferred to the hospital and material damage occurred, though details were not provided. This incident follows Kuwait activating its air defense system last week to counter Iranian drone attacks.

item.title: US-Led Consortium Reaches Agreement to Acquire Lukoil's International Assets
item.description: A consortium of investors, including the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), has agreed to acquire Lukoil's international assets. The deal involves acquiring Lukoil International, which holds non-Russian energy assets in 11 countries. The consortium will exchange Russian shares for Lukoil International's liquidity, avoiding direct cash payments to Russia. The DFC's participation aims to protect US interests.

item.title: Kazakhstan Interior Ministry Warns of Road Dangers Due to Worsening Weather
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs has urged drivers and pedestrians to exercise caution due to deteriorating weather conditions in several regions. Police advise adhering to safety measures and avoiding intercity travel if possible, as heavy rain, snow, strong winds, and ice are expected.

item.title: Uzbekistan National Bank Plans Significant Financial Support for Economy and Entrepreneurship
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Bank plans to allocate 38.5 trillion soums in loans this year, supporting economic sectors and entrepreneurship. The bank has already directed 15 trillion soums to key industries and 1.7 trillion to construction projects. Special focus is on youth entrepreneurship, aiming to create jobs for 10,000 more young people.

item.title: 75 kg of Meat Contaminated with Dangerous Bacteria Destroyed in North Kazakhstan
item.description: Seventy-five kilograms of frozen meat found to be contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes bacteria have been destroyed by burning in the North Kazakhstan region. The violation was detected during a market monitoring project. The Ministry of Trade and Integration emphasized the responsibility of entrepreneurs for product safety.

item.title: Fergana Region's Economic Development and Income Growth Priorities Identified
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev chaired a meeting on enhancing reforms, accelerating industrial development, and increasing incomes in the Fergana region. The region expects 9.6% GDP growth, 8.5% industrial growth, and 16.3% service sector growth this year. Discussions focused on untapped potential and new investment projects in energy, construction materials, electrical engineering, and pharmaceuticals.

item.title: Prospects for Cooperation Between Central Asia and Europe Outlined at Berlin Conference
item.description: Eldor Aripov, Director of the Institute for Strategic and Regional Studies of Uzbekistan, participated in the Berlin Conference 2026, discussing strategic autonomy for Europe. He highlighted the improved atmosphere of trust and good neighborliness in Central Asia, driven by Uzbekistan's policies, and outlined approaches for dialogue between Central Asia and European states.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Chamber of Accounts May Audit World Bank Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan's Chamber of Accounts met with World Bank representatives to discuss improving its operations and adopting international audit standards. The Chamber, transitioning to international standards, has gained authority to audit projects funded by international financial institutions. The World Bank positively assessed the first audit of the "EduImkon" program.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Urges Training for Rural Internet Income Generation
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has called for reducing the digital divide and training rural residents to earn income online. He emphasized that smartphones, with proper use, can be a tool for financial independence in villages, fostering a 'people's digital economy'.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses Priorities for Tourism Potential and Cultural Heritage Preservation
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed a presentation on tourism development and future priorities, focusing on major projects in Bukhara. Tasks were set for restoring cultural heritage sites, preserving the historical city's character, and enhancing tourist appeal, including plans for the Ark museum-reserve and Samanid Park.

item.title: UN Special Rapporteur Urges Justice and Support for Afghan Survivors of Violence
item.description: Richard Bennett, the UN Special Rapporteur on human rights in Afghanistan, called for justice and support for survivors of violence on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. He emphasized the importance of the 16 Days of Activism campaign for ending impunity and supporting Afghan women and girls' right to live free from gender-based violence.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Ancient Cities May Become Hollywood Film Locations
item.description: Hollywood producer Larry Kasanoff suggested that Samarkand, Bukhara, and Khiva could serve as filming locations for Hollywood movies. A memorandum of cooperation in cinema and tourism was signed, aiming to promote Uzbekistan's heritage and natural potential for international film productions, including a potential adventure blockbuster.

item.title: Taliban Plan to Convert Mullah Mohammad Omar's Zabul Residence into Museum
item.description: Local sources report the Taliban intend to transform Mullah Mohammad Omar's former residence in Zabul Province into a museum. A delegation from the Ministry of Information and Culture has visited the site for preliminary assessments. Millions have reportedly been spent on renovating Omar's grave.

item.title: Pakistan and Netherlands Discuss Militant Groups' Presence in Afghanistan
item.description: Pakistan's special representative for Afghanistan, Mohammad Sadiq Khan, met with Dutch officials in Islamabad to discuss regional security and the presence of militant groups in Afghanistan. They referenced UN reports and Kabul's rejection of such allegations.

item.title: Tokayev and Putin Meet Young AI Talents at Conference
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Russia's President Vladimir Putin met with young participants at the AI Journey 2026 conference. Tokayev congratulated the AI Olympiad winners, emphasizing the elder generation's role in creating conditions for their professional growth, which is of state importance for economic development and security.

item.title: Tokayev and Putin Discuss Future of AI with Students and Schoolchildren
item.description: Presidents Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Vladimir Putin discussed the future of artificial intelligence with students and schoolchildren from Kazakhstan, Russia, and India. The meeting, held at the AI Journey 2026 conference, focused on how AI will transform science, medicine, education, economy, and art.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev proposes joint AI projects for Russian schoolchildren
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev suggested launching joint educational projects with Russia focused on artificial intelligence for schoolchildren and teachers. Speaking at the AI Journey 2026 conference in Moscow, he emphasized the importance of critical thinking and independent analysis in the age of AI.

item.title: Trump and NATO Secretary-General Discuss Ukraine War, Iran Conflicts, and Defense Spending
item.description: US President Donald Trump met with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte to discuss the war in Ukraine, conflicts involving Iran, and increased defense spending by NATO members. Trump described the meeting as highly successful and impactful, emphasizing the need for a peaceful resolution to the Ukraine conflict.

item.title: Bishkek Investment Forum Aims to Become Year-Round Platform, Discusses China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway
item.description: The Bishkek Investment Forum (BIF) aims to transform into a year-round investment platform with an online portal and an "Invest Club." This year's forum attracted over a thousand business representatives and investors. A key discussion point was the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project and its potential benefits for small and medium-sized businesses.

item.title: UN Experts Urge Inclusive Justice and Rights Guarantees for Afghan Victims
item.description: UN experts emphasize the need for inclusive and comprehensive justice for victims of crimes in Afghanistan, ensuring their rights to truth, justice, and reparation. Efforts to achieve justice for persecution of women and girls must align with addressing other serious crimes. Victims' courage should not be met with abandonment, and clear information must be provided.
